notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

DDR200, the SD card's fastest mode, is now tested per card. Settings, Performance,
SD Card measures your card at standard speed, then restarts once into DDR200 to
measure it again and check it under load, about three minutes. A popup then shows
both speed runs, the retried errors per GB, any reads or writes that failed and any
data that came back wrong. DDR200 is recommended when the card reads at least 10
percent faster, with no wrong data, no failed reads or writes and under 3 retried
errors per GB, and you choose to keep it or go back to standard speed. A card that
only missed the error limit can still be forced on.

DDR200 is now off for every card until it is tested. Samsung cards used to get it by
their maker, but one gave errors under load in testing while other makers' cards can
pass, so test yours to turn it back on. While DDR200 is on, SCCM Retro checks for
errors outside games and turns it off at the next restart if a recommended card goes
clearly over the limit or a read or write fails.

PS2 games no longer start with settings notices in the top-left corner, and turning
the emulator stats overlay off now clears all of its lines. Loading a PS2 save state
no longer prints memory card messages. A game can still show its own "memory card
removed" screen when the state is older than its last save; that is the game noticing
its card was refreshed, which protects the saves on it.

PSP games on the standalone PPSSPP engine now show the emulator FPS overlay. On ports,
3DS and DraStic games, which have no counter of their own, the pause menu's
Performance overlay switch now shows the stats overlay with one press.

During CPU, GPU and RAM tuning, the tuning screen now shows from the start of every
restart instead of the boot splash, so a running test no longer looks frozen.

SCCM Retro now asks once whether to share anonymous hardware data to improve
performance and compatibility: chip grades, the RAM module, tuner results, the SD
card and its DDR200 results, the Switch model and screens. No personal data. Change
your answer, or see exactly what is sent, in Settings, Contributions.

The Overclocking section of Settings is now called Performance.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu has a new icon and can add SCCM Retro to the
Home menu (this needs sigpatches), and fresh installs from it start on the newest
release.

The DDR200 test was tried on one console with a Samsung card, and the hardware data
on another. If a card freezes during the DDR200 test, hold Power to restart; it comes
back at standard speed. The Home menu shortcut has not been tried on a console yet.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
